LLM auditresponse for zfs-file-history.install:
<security_assessment>
  <decision>SAFE</decision>
  <details>
    The file is an AUR install script for the zfs-file-history package. It defines three helper functions - _zfs_file_history_upgrade_notes, _zfs_file_history_print_notes, and _zfs_file_history_flush - and a post_upgrade hook. The script reads lines from standard input, identifies entries starting with ==, and prints formatted upgrade notes using cat, vercmp, sed and while read. No external commands such as curl, wget or git pull are invoked. Although the source contains HTML entity markers that resemble less-than and greater-than symbols, these are merely artifacts of the original encoding and do not affect execution. The script follows typical AUR packaging patterns: it pulls content from the upstream repository (the markusressel/zfs-file-history project) via the existing packaging/aur/publish.sh workflow, and emits a link to full releases when needed. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, code execution from untrusted hosts, or injection of arbitrary code. Minor hygiene considerations include reliance on the vercmp utility (common on Debian based systems) and the use of a heredoc delimiter named NOTES. Neither constitutes a security problem. The script performs only local file operations (printing to stdout) and does not modify system files outside its own scope. Overall it behaves like ordinary packaging code for a third-party utility.
  </details>
  <evidence></evidence>
  <summary>Standard AUR packaging script, no malicious behavior detected.</summary>
</security_assessment>
